title: N119 in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: The H II region N119 in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope
celestial: N 119 · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This picture shows N119, a glowing cloud of gas in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring galaxy about 170,000 light-years away. Its most unusual feature is a pronounced spiral shape that recalls a barred spiral galaxy, even though N119 is a nebula, not a galaxy.

N119 is an H II region, a cloud of hydrogen gas lit by hot young stars. Their energetic light strips electrons from the hydrogen atoms, and the gas glows as the atoms recapture them. The image includes a filter tuned to that hydrogen glow.

The nebula is large and sits in an interesting place. It lies on the northern side of the Large Magellanic Cloud's stellar bar, a long band of stars across the galaxy, close to the center around which the galaxy's neutral hydrogen rotates. That bar is also why the lower half of the field is packed with many more stars than the upper half.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (31.49 x 30.64 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 1,600 × 1,500 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope took this visible-light image through B, V and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The hydrogen filter and long exposures reveal glowing gas far too faint for the eye to see.

explore: N119 measures about 400 by 600 light-years. The image was made with the Wide Field Imager through blue, visual and hydrogen-alpha filters.
alt: A glowing nebula with a spiral shape among many stars, denser in the lower half.
